extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and journalists interested in wartime news and propaganda
extracted.subtask_description: Contemporary newspaper reporting on WWII events, including discussion of propaganda tactics and how the British handle Axis misinformation. Focused on conveying factual events and on methods for countering enemy propaganda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty as counter-propaganda principle
rubrics_metrics.description: British counter-propaganda adopts the motto 'honesty is the best policy' rather than broad denials or fabrications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article explains that the British respond to enemy lies by presenting factual, unsensational truth; they avoid outright denials and prefer to treat items positively (i.e., report what actually happened) so as to undercut false enemy claims. Example: when Germans said the King and Queen had fled to Canada, the British 'merely broadcast what the King and Queen had done that day.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote enemy statements with dry comment (technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practical technique is to quote Axis or enemy declarations and present them with minimal or dry commentary rather than issuing blunt refutations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece notes this technique as 'highly effective' — e.g., carrying German versions of events with dry comment (as in the Dieppe raid coverage) so the enemy's own words reveal inconsistencies or absurdities without amplifying propaganda. Use of the enemy's statements lets readers judge credibility and exposes contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and treat enemy propaganda tactics skeptically
rubrics_metrics.description: Be alert to specific enemy propaganda maneuvers: deliberate exaggeration, reversing casualty/loss figures, mixing truth with falsehoods, and half-truths that omit unfavorable parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists examples of Axis tactics — exaggerating plane losses, reversing figures of plane losses (making 19/9 into 9/19), and combining some true elements with false ones to lend plausibility. Guidance is to treat such claims skeptically and to counter them by factual reporting, indirect treatment, or exposing internal inconsistencies rather than repeating them uncritically.
